entries.summary: Quang Ba Flower Market is flowers before breakfast: bundles, wet pavement, scooters, vendors moving fast, and a quieter city still waking up.
entries.context: Quảng Bá belongs to Hanoi before sunrise, when flowers move by bundle and scooter for real homes, shops, and ceremonies.
entries.tip: Stand aside for a minute before buying or taking photos. The market has lanes, pace, and working hands to respect.
entries.rationale: Chợ hoa Quảng Bá stays vivid through flowers, wet pavement, scooters, and working-market pace rather than fixed specifics about timing or price.

sections.title: Flowers Before Breakfast
sections.body: Quảng Bá is bundles of flowers, wet pavement, scooters, and vendors moving while much of Hanoi is still quiet.

sections.title: Work Before Photos
sections.body: Stand aside before entering a stall lane. The market has its own rhythm, and the flowers are moving for real buyers.

sections.title: Chợ Hoa Quảng Bá Before Dawn
sections.body: Chợ hoa Quảng Bá is the name to connect with Hanoi's early flower trade near the lake side.

sections.title: Small Bundle Logic
sections.body: If buying flowers, think about the rest of the morning. A small bundle travels better than a fragile armful.

sections.title: Lake Morning
sections.body: The market pairs naturally with a West Lake-side morning, coffee afterward, or a slow ride back into the city.

sections.title: Morning Rhythm Changes
sections.body: Early hours, light browsing, and a working-market pace fit the scene: flowers moving, scooters passing, wet pavement underfoot.

entries.summary: The Red River opens Hanoi at the waterline: Long Bien Bridge above, sandy banks below, boats, reflections, and working water stretching the city wider.
entries.context: The Red River gives Hanoi its older waterline, with bridges, sandy banks, working boats, and a sense of the city stretching beyond the lake district.
entries.tip: See the river from Long Bien Bridge first. The banks, distance, and working water make more sense from that frame.
entries.rationale: Sông Hồng organizes the river view around safer frames, working water, and changeable bank conditions.

sections.title: City At The Waterline
sections.body: The Red River is working water, bridge steel, sandy banks, boats, reflections, and a wider edge to Hanoi.

sections.title: Long Bien First
sections.body: Long Bien Bridge gives the river shape. From there, banks, boats, and distance read better than from a random road edge.

sections.title: Sông Hồng Beside The Bridges
sections.body: Sông Hồng is the Vietnamese name for the Red River, useful when water views, bridge crossings, and north-side routes enter the day.

sections.title: Working Banks
sections.body: Do not treat every open patch as a promenade. Stay aware of footing, traffic, and where local movement actually goes.

sections.title: Light Over Distance
sections.body: The river rewards a simple plan: one bridge view, one waterline pause, then a clear way back.

sections.title: Banks Are Uneven
sections.body: The river view is strongest when kept simple: bridge angles, water, haze, and a clear way back from uncertain edges.

entries.summary: St. Joseph's Cathedral sits where old lanes, scooters, cafe umbrellas, and a tall stone facade press into one central square near Hoan Kiem.
entries.context: St. Joseph's Cathedral belongs to the old-lane city around Hoàn Kiếm, where a Gothic facade, cafe tables, scooters, and church bells share one square.
entries.tip: Give the cathedral its own pause before turning toward coffee. The surrounding streets make distraction easy.
entries.rationale: Nhà thờ Lớn Hà Nội is a specific sacred landmark, with respectful visit behavior shaped by services, square life, and old lanes.

sections.title: Old Lanes, Big Facade
sections.body: The cathedral gathers stone, scooters, cafe umbrellas, passing people, and old lanes into one compact square.

sections.title: Square Before Door
sections.body: The outside is part of the stop: facade, street movement, people waiting, and cafes around the edges.

sections.title: Nhà Thờ Lớn By The Square
sections.body: Nhà thờ Lớn Hà Nội is the Vietnamese name to connect with the cathedral square and nearby old lanes.

sections.title: Worship Stays Clear
sections.body: If the doors are open, gentle doorway manners matter. Prayer, quiet, and doorway space should stay protected.

sections.title: Coffee Can Wait
sections.body: Nearby cafes are tempting, but the cathedral deserves ten minutes of its own before the next cup.

sections.title: Service Times Matter
sections.body: The square, worship mood, and nearby old lanes set the pace. A respectful pause beats crowding the doorway for a photo.

entries.summary: A Hanoi street-food walk is a meal across short stops: steam from a pot, herbs on a tray, low stools, and a grill before the next corner.
entries.context: A street-food walk belongs to Hanoi because meals often unfold across small stops: steam here, herbs there, low stools, then a sweet finish.
entries.tip: Order one dish per stop when possible. A bowl, plate, or shared portion leaves room for the next smell or corner.
entries.rationale: Đi bộ ăn vặt Hà Nội guides food-walk behavior through small orders, short distances, and a route loose enough to follow the evening.

sections.title: A Meal Across Stops
sections.body: A street-food walk is steam, herbs, low stools, grilled smoke, and small decisions spaced across several short stops.

sections.title: Small Orders
sections.body: One dish per stop keeps the night open. A bowl of pho, a plate of bánh cuốn, or shared bún chả can be enough.

sections.title: Đi Bộ Ăn Vặt
sections.body: Đi bộ ăn vặt Hà Nội is the phrase for a casual Hanoi food walk built from small stops.

sections.title: Busy Tables
sections.body: A line of people finishing bowls says more than a bright sign. Watch for fresh herbs and cooks already moving.

sections.title: Sweet Ending
sections.body: Leave room for egg coffee, fruit, or a small dessert so the walk slows down instead of ending heavy.

sections.title: Vendor Mix Changes
sections.body: Smoke, stools, queues, and appetite should shape the walk. Small orders leave room for the evening to adjust.

entries.summary: Ta Hien is the Old Quarter at evening volume: low stools, warm signs, food smoke, bia hơi, and groups deciding how long the night should go.
entries.context: Tạ Hiện belongs to the Old Quarter's evening release, where low stools, beer, smoke, and compressed lanes turn the street into a shared room.
entries.tip: Read the menu board and prices before sitting. The street gets louder as the night goes on, so simple questions are easier early.
entries.rationale: Phố Tạ Hiện captures the social evening lane while bar, price, crowd-control, and opening details stay changeable.

sections.title: One Lap Before A Stool
sections.body: Tạ Hiện is low stools, warm signs, food smoke, bia hơi, and groups deciding whether the night is one drink or several streets.

sections.title: Earlier Evening Read
sections.body: Dusk makes the lane easier to read. You can compare seats, food, beer, music, and crowd level before committing.

sections.title: Tạ Hiện After Dark
sections.body: Phố Tạ Hiện is the street name to pair with Old Quarter nightlife, low stools, and warm evening signs.

sections.title: Prices Before Bottles
sections.body: Read the menu board and drink prices before you sit. The money question is simpler before the street gets loud.

sections.title: Exit Before It Drags
sections.body: The charm is compression. When noise stops feeling fun, step toward the lake or another Old Quarter lane.

sections.title: Night Conditions Change
sections.body: Read the block once before sitting down: crowd pressure, parked bikes, bar entrances, and where you can step aside.
